projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Lawrence H. Vogel was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: ___+ Historical Museum located on 7 Day Street in Fredonia, New York 14063. Phone Number 716-672-2114, and today is November 29th, 2001. Today we are here with Lawrence Vogel. How are you Lawrence?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Fine.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Would you like to tell us your name? Even though I just said it.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Lawrence H. Vogel.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: And your birth date?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: [birth date redacted].

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: And your current address?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Laughing} What is my current address? Is it--what is it?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: [address redacted]?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yep.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah. In Dunkirk.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: New York. Okay. The wars in which you served?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: World War II and the Korean War.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. And your branch of service?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Quartermaster.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: And you were in the--Army?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Right. Army.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. Do you remember your highest rank?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Master Sergeant.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Master Sergeant. I guess, as we get into your--this interview, I was wondering if you'd like to tell us your most vivid memory of your wartime experience?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, the most vivid would be when we landed at Normandy, and the experiences I had through the European Theater of operations which included Sicily also. And then we landed at Sicily and--let me see if I remember--North Africa, Sicily, and then Normandy. World War II. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What stuck out about Normandy?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Not much. Just run like hell so you didn't get hit.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing} Did you run pretty fast?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Fast as I could. {Gesturing and sound effects of running while smiling}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What can you tell us about the military life and culture? Was there a difference, like, between--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, it's a lot different than from civilian society, but I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you? How come?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Because when I was younger, I wanted to get into the military, really.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And--they--I enlisted, and that's how they got me into the service. See?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How long did you serve?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, I guess, overall, I think it was 22 years. It was five regular Army service, and the rest of it, 17 years, in the National Guard.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. What about, you know, in talking about military life, what were the rations like? In--were they different between World War II and the Korean conflict?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, World War II was altogether different. I mean, we were activated, and then we were sent overseas. See, I was overseas for five years during World War II. Whereas, in the Korean, I didn't get into active service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, I was activated but we never--I never went overseas.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Where did you stay during the Korean War? Do you remember?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I think most of the time it was down in Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: In Jersey.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And I think later on, we went down to Florida. I forget--there's some military outfit down in Florida. We stayed there. I think it was Fort Jackson. I'm not really positive.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. Did you get wounded? Were you wounded?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, later on I found a bullet hole through my field jacket. {Indicating his right arm} That's the closest I come to-- {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Was that World War II?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I think I got that at Normandy.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So it was close, huh?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. {Nodding} You had to run like hell. {Gesturing and sound effects of running while smiling}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: When you were in the European Theater during World War II did--what was--what was--what were the living conditions like? Were you always on the move, or did you sleep in tents? Do--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Most of it--well, quite a--a couple of years were in England where we trained. And then we landed in Normandy, and we went through the whole campaign, and I ended up in--Czechoslovakia.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Czech--Czechoslovakia. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And then after that, we went back to the States, and I stayed in the service. And then during the Korean, I was activated for--I think about two and a half years, but I didn't go out of the States during the Korean War.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I think most of my time was down in Fort Dix and Fort Bliss, Texas.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So during World War II, you experienced combat, but in the Korean War you didn't?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. You do that when you hit three landings.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: You're in combat. {Laughing and nodding}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What were the landings like? Did you--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: So-the what?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: The landings. What were the landings like?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: They're real smooth.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: You jumped out of the boats and run like hell through the--what little bit of water and-- {Nodding} then once you got in them--why, then you get to a routine process.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Where--were you on the boats very long?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. It took us about two weeks to get across. We were--we weren't on one of these--no. I'll take that back. We were on the Queen Mary when we first went over. It took us maybe five or six days. There was 30,000 troops on that ship.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh, my. Must have been a big boat?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yes, the Queen Mary is a big boat. Then during the Korean--oh, where did I spend my time? Probably down in Fort Dix too. But I didn't do overseas during the Korean War.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right. Do you remember what kind of boats you were on when you did the landing? They have a name?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Queen Mary.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh, but after that. Because you said you--you did three landings. Were there other--do you remember the other boats? Or--I mean, it's okay if you don't. But--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Incidentally--just in case--a lot of people don't know this I don't think. There was two divisions of troops on the Queen Mary.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: There was a steady line going back and forth in ___? When you have 30,000 troops on one ship--a lot of people don't know that that ship could hold that many, but it did.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah. I didn't know that.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And it was a five-day trip across, and during the Korean War, I was down in--I think down either--somewhere in Virginia or North Carolina. I don't recall right off, but I didn't go overseas during the Korean War.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right. Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: See, they yanked me in for two years for the National Guard.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But I finished out my 20--22 years overall service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you make any friends in either of ____?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, yeah. I made a lot of friends.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But you had to leave them.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: It was--actually, it was nice. It was--I enjoyed myself. I think maybe a lot of people didn't, but I did. I enjoyed myself in the service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: In both World War II and Korea or just in World War II?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Both.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Both.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I mean, I enjoyed myself in the Army. Otherwise, I wouldn't have joined. See?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Because I didn't--actually, I didn't want to wait--wait to be drafted. I wanted to get in and see what it was like which I did. I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How old were you when you--

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: When you started?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh. Do you still keep in touch with your friends that you made?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Very few.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Very few. Do you want to mention any of their names?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: They're all--oh, gosh. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: I know. Okay. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Laughing} I can't think of any of their names. There were so many and--to tell you the truth, I have--I really can't think of--I can't think of a name of one of them right now. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Well, it's kind of a little pressure with the camera, huh?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Okay. But the most experience I liked was when down in--we were down in Czechoslovakia. Most of the soldiers stayed in homes.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Luckily, I got a nice home. Boy, the food was great and everything. I really enjoyed that.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So you stayed with a family? Did they have children?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. They had--well, they were grown-up children. I think they had two boys and one daughter, but it--it was a lot of fun. I--I enjoyed my service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What kind of food did you get?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Good food.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Good food?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Good, wholesome food. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Different or similar to what we have here in the States?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, similar to what we have, but it was--it mostly was simple food, but it was good.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And--I had no complaints.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Was their home different than the types of homes we have here?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. They're similar to ours. Like the family--I was with a family--they had the husband and wife. They had one son and one daughter and two dogs. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: A Dachshund.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh, Dachshunds? Yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did--do you remember their names?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: No?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I--I couldn't remember any. I know. The other day I was thinking I better look over my stuff and see-- I'm pretty sure I had names in there and everything, but I'll have to check with my son, George, and see. I hope he's got that stuff. Yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But I enjoyed my service in the Army.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I jumped in the water three times, but that--that was nothing. I got out of it. A lot--a lot of poor guys didn't get out of it, but fortunately, I did. {Clears throat}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What was your least favorite thing?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: The who?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Your least favorite? I mean, we--you were just talking about your favorite--one of your favorite things being the people you stayed with. What were your least favorite? I mean, if you want to share it.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. We only stayed--I think--in England I think we stayed at a post or a fort over in England.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But in Czechoslovakia and mostly overseas, we stayed with families.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And it was very enjoyable. No problem.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: They're just like us.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh, yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But--I'm glad for the experience really.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. Did you--did you have any favorite musical hits?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Musical hits?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah. Music. Was there any music you remember from that time that you liked or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Pausing} Yeah. Mostly--I guess a lot of people would call it "high-bred" music. You know, opera and stuff like that that.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And--the modern hits. I mean I--I like those too. Every time they got, you know, the hit parade and all that stuff we used to have, you know. They were great.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Inez (ph) wrote me a little note asking me to mention about if you would tell us about how you met your wife?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: That was the greatest experience of my life really. {Laughing} See, when we were over in--New England. This is just--Nashville, New Hampshire. We stayed in private homes. And I met her at--oh, what the heck were they? Oh, what do you call those dances they had--the Army--gosh, I can't think of the name of it now, but I met her at a dance in Nashville, New Hampshire.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And I eventually married her. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing} Is that a picture of her? On the chair?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Huh?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Is that--that--there's--is that a picture of her on the chair? Next to you? Underneath there was a little picture. Is that her?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Reaching over next to him} Yeah. That's Helen.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Do you want to hold it up so we can see?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Holding picture to camera} That was her. She was in the "wax."

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What's that?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: The WAVES--Navy.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh. Is she--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Can't think what the--what the "wax" were--no, no. Not the "wax," the WAVES.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: The WAVES?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah, the WAVES.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Do you know how long she served?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: About two years.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Two years?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Two years in the WAVES.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What did she do?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, what did they do? Well, she worked mostly as a--sort of nursing in the hospitals and stuff like that down in--Washington D.C., and that was most of their duties, the WAVES. Well, the whites, too, in the Army.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. She was a wonderful person. We got married, had four children, and then she died in 1992, but we had a good life together.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So she was in the service when you met her--as well?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. I met her at a dance. Oh, what the heck was that city I told you in New Hampshire again? It was around the capitol of New Hampshire--dog gone it--Nashville, New Hampshire.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: It's about 30,000 population, and her folks were farm folks, and I met her at a dance. USO dance.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh, that's it. USO dance.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: That did it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing} Do you remember what songs you danced to?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, she died in 1992.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: We had four children. One died, but three children are still alive. One's in California, one's around Boston, Mass., and George is down in Concord.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No, I had a good life.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: That's good. Inez (ph) has also asked me to ask about your rations in combat.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: The only action I had in combat was three landings. We landed Normandy--6:00 o'clock in the morning we landed. We landed--I was with the 1st U.S. Infantry Division.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Then we made a landing in Sicily--North Africa and Sicily and then Normandy. So we all knew our landings.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What about--what about the rations?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I liked it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: The food in combat?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I liked it. A lot of them dummies didn't for some odd--they must have been fussy eaters. Because it was good food.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Don't let anybody tell you any different. Those rations were real good, solid food. And if anybody says anything against them, you tell them I said he's a nut.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing} I guess--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: See, those C-Rations--what they call C-Rations--

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Uh-huh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: That's was when troops are out in the field. What the heck was the other one now? I can't think of the other one. C-Rations were mostly of canned food and dried food--crackers and stuff like that. That was your lowest type of rations. But--no. The food is great in the Army. Don't let anybody--and if anybody tells you about ___ food, he was a fussy eater. It was wholesome food.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Are there any other stories you can think of about your time in service that you want to share with us? Any funny stories, or any--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, my greatest was ___ was when I met my wife, like I say, in Nashville, New Hampshire, at a dance.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And eventually we'd get married. But, no. I--they had a lot of activities in the Army, and I enjoyed all of them. I enjoyed the Army, but there's a lot of guys that didn't. Now, why, I can't figure their--I don't know. Somehow or another they were--they were mad because they were drafted. See I--I enlisted. I wanted to be in the service, and I had seven years active. They--they hooked me back in in 40--during the Korean War for two years, but that didn't bother me any, and the rest of the years was nice, and I retired. So I got a good pension out of it. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What did your family think when you--enlisted?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, during the Korean War--well, I was married then.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Of course, she didn't--she took it. She was in the WAVES too.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: My wife was in the WAVES so she knew what it was all like.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And, no. There was no fussing.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Even when you enlisted when you were a young man?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: No?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I was 18 when I enlisted, and I knew they were going to get me. I didn't want to be drafted. See, I wanted to go in by myself and go in the outfit I wanted to go in, which I did.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So you had a choice then?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How neat.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Then I got a lot of schooling in the service. I went to quite a few schools in the service which helped me when I got out of the service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What did you do when you got out of the service?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I worked in the State Army for about 23 years. Then I was in the National Guard for 20-some years. So--I wanted those three pensions, which I got. And a lot of guys got out, and I don't know how--how they're doing now. They're probably in a poor house a lot of them. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: And so your family was supportive when you enlisted?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, yeah. Yeah. No problem.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you have brothers and sisters?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. I--actually, my original family, there was seven, seven brothers and one sister.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But they were all grown up. My twin brother joined the Marines. I joined the Army. I had a brother join the Air Force, and I think--what the heck--what the heck was the other one? There was four of us--Army, Navy, Air Force--oh, one brother was a chaplain.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh. In the service?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: In the Army?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Nodding} And he had a good parish right till he died at--oh, what's the name of it? Saint--a parish in West Seneca (ph) he started.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh. Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: So he's on his way. He died. I think--I--right now I think I have two brothers left. I had seven brothers and one sister.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: But every--it sounds like a lot of your brothers went into the service--or branch--a different branch of the service?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Four of us did.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How did your brother like the Marines?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, he enjoyed it. He stayed in the Marines and when he--he--after the war he did like I did. He went in the reserves. We got our three pensions. That's what I went for, and I enjoyed the service. A lot of guys didn't. I can't figure it out.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Maybe they didn't like the food as much as you?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Pardon?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Maybe they didn't like the food as much? {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, if they didn't, they lied.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: The food was good. I don't care what you say. The food was good and wholesome. Let's put it this way: The guys that were in the service had better food than when they were back home with their families. Because it was nourish--real nourish--nourishable [sic] food, not junk food. No. I've got nothing against the service.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Now--oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How do you feel--that all this has impacted your life?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, actually, I say it--it made my life more enjoyable. All the experiences--places I went. I went through all of Europe, North Africa, Sicily. I couldn't afford any of that. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Why were you in North Africa? Do you remember?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, that was the first place we landed in North Africa. It was with the 1st U.S. Infantry Division, and they were first in any landing.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And see, we had an--we have to--the Germans occupied all those territories and that was--that was the most vulnerable one. I mean, that's the way I looked at it. I mean, there wasn't much resistance at all--North Africa, Sicily--but Normandy was a little bit different. A lot of--a lot of guys got killed there in that thing but--yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What do you remember about Africa? Was it hot or dry or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: It's beautiful country. As a matter of fact, I wouldn't mind living down there, if I so desired. But--no. The weather down there is beautiful. There's places there just like ours here, like, ___. It's a beautiful country. It's all mountains. The people were nice. They were mostly French in North Africa. A lot of English, German, but I think, most generally, I'd say French dominated, but they were nice people. They were very nice to us.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What about Sicily? Do you remember that?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: That was great too. That was--see, mostly Italians--mostly Italians down in Sicily, but see, Sicily they call the pearl, the green pearl of the Mediterranean. It's a beautiful, beautiful island.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: At that time, there was hardly any manufacturers. Mostly agricultural people, religious people, mostly all Catholics down through there. I mean, I'm not rubbing the--the other religions.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But they were really, really nice people. I never ran across a group of people during the Army ___, and they enjoyed us, too, I think, too. They were real happy with us. And that's--we liberated a lot of them. See?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But--no. I enjoyed--I enjoyed myself. Of course, a lot of guys were grumbling, but they'd grumble any place.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you in--in all your travels, did you get up to Germany itself or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, yeah.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah? What was your impression?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: We went through France, Germany, Czechoslovakia. We ended up in Czechoslovakia. That's the tip of Czechoslovakia. They're a wonderful people. Didn't run across any people that hated us.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Except maybe the English. {Laughing} When we were over in England.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did you--{laughing} when you were--how long--did--do you know how much time you spent in Germany or--was it very long or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, maybe about six months. It didn't take us long to get through there, but we stayed there. Mostly--mostly we were--we ended up in Czechoslovakia.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What were you doing in Czechoslovakia?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Occupation mostly.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Occupation?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: It wasn't much fighting--once we got through Germany. They were the ones that slowed us up. But once we got through that Nazi situation, there was no problem. Everybody welcomed us really.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What were--so you faced a lot of--of combat in Germany--as well?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No, not too much. The most combat we had was on the three landings really.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Of course, there were a few pockets of resistance, but they didn't last too long.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How did you guys usually travel? Did you go by train or car or, you know, tank or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Mostly truck.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Mostly truck?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Army trucks.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Was that comfortable?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yep. It ran pretty good.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. Jeeps, station wagons {laughing} ___, but--no. I loved the Army. I stayed in for 23 years.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But most of it--well, let's see. I had about seven years active during the World War II, and the Korean War they called me back, but that didn't bother me any. I was married and had three children, and I enjoyed going back, and my wife was with me too. I mean, she wasn't with me, but she wasn't against me, like a lot of wives would be.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: She was supportive?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: They were very, very supportive. I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Do you want to show us your other picture? Your other photograph on the chair? The big one?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, that one there. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Here. Hold it up so Michael can get a close-up.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Holding up picture} That was Fort Bliss, Texas.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Was that Korean or World War II?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: World War II before we went overseas. Training. We trained down there in Fort Bliss. That's right at the Mexican border. Where--right across from Fort Bliss was the city of Juarez in Mexico.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And--no. It was very enjoyable down here, and we got a lot of-- {speaking to camera person} you all through? Camera Person: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: We have--see, you go across the Rio Grande. It's right on the Rio Grande. So once you cross the bridge there--at Rio Grande to Juarez, Mexico--everything's real cheap in Mexico.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I don't know whether it is now. For instance, in--oh, what the name of that city I was in there, in across from Juarez--dang it. Across the Mexican--American side--you'd pay about five, seven dollars for a good meal. You go to Juarez, you can get the same meal, just about, for two and a half dollars. That was the difference.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And boy, we swarmed across those bridges. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: It was a lot of fun.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Was it easy for you guys to get across or--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, yeah. It cost a nickel to walk over the bridge to Juarez, and 10 cents to walk from Juarez to El Paso, Texas. But--no. We got a lot of souvenirs and different things from across the Rio Grande.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: How long were you there about in Fort Bliss?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Oh, about six or eight months I think it was. I was glad to get out of there, but it was nice. It was nice duty really. No. If anybody goes in the service, they've got to make their minds up to enjoy it. If not--they've got to-- {shaking head} they're in it, and they know they're in it. They should make, you know, good use of their time and everything--not with a lot of grumbles and stuff like that. But I think the majority like it to tell you the truth.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Yeah. Do you have a message for future generations?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, they should enjoy themselves, behave themselves, and stay out of trouble, {smiling} but--that's hard for a lot of Americans. But if you ever do a lot of traveling overseas, you will see the difference between the American way of life or wherever you're at. Because anywhere you go almost today, it's over populated, and that's the difference. But I enjoyed it. I don't know about a lot of people didn't, but it's too bad. You're in it. You're there. Enjoy yourselves. That's the way I look at it. I liked the armed service. I stayed in for--well, I had seven years active duty, and the rest was National Guard. I--I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Did--did you receive any medals or special awards?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. The occasions didn't arise. The only medals, I guess, when we landed at Normandy and North Africa and Sicily. I was in the ordinance, I wasn't in any infantry or artillery or anything like that. See, most of your medals go to your infantry men because they're in the front lines.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Of course a lot of them got some medals for different things. And--no. I--I did like ___ and whatever came with it. That was it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: What was your main job? Do you remember? Did you have, like, a certain specific job that you had to do?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. I was--well, I was called the 1st Quartermaster Battalion.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I don't know if you know anything about a Quartermaster Battalion?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Nope. Please tell us.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: That battalion serves the rest of the troops in the division, and they work hard. That is, they get the food to them--the clothes to them. Like, I was in the motor--I was in a motorized outfit.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: And we repaired trucks, Jeeps, and stuff like that. Then you had the medical outfit. They took care of the medical. The medical company. Then it became a medical battalion, and that served all the medical supplies there for the whole division. At that time the division was 12,000 troops. So that's a job to keep stuff like that going.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: So you were responsible for doing a lot--helping keep the motorized--

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Yeah. I worked re-tiring trucks and stuff like that. Yeah, I was a motor mechanic, and that was a lot of fun. I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Trucks?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I don't know about the majority, but I enjoyed my time in the service. I had seven years active, and the rest was National Guard. I stayed in--it's too bad these kids were--they got involved, and they should have enjoyed themselves, but they bucked it. Just like a lot of kids today. They don't want to serve in the service. I don't--I can't figure out why. It's too bad.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Seems to me, sometimes people are afraid. So you must have had a lot of courage.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Well, I wouldn't call it courage. I enjoyed myself. I did what I was supposed to do. That's all, and that's what--everything that matters. That's in civilian life too.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No matter what you do in civilian life, you do what you're supposed to do, the best you can, and that's the way you get anywhere. You got a lot of loafers in civilian life too. Don't ever forget that. {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Oh. So--so were you ever afraid? Were there times you were afraid?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: Not really.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: No? Not even at Normandy?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Just run, huh?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: You did your job. A lot of people were killed. A lot of people were wounded. I got a bullet through my jacket, but I didn't even know I had that until I got back from my service, you know? {Laughing} But--no. I can imagine a lot of people that didn't want to get in the service, but when they got in there, they should have enjoyed themselves and did the best they could, but I think a lot of them bucked it and got in trouble. That's the problem. I enjoyed my service. I had a lot of fun doing it. I got paid for it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: What more could you ask?

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: The food was good.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: {Laughing}

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Pointing a finger} Now, if anybody complains to you about Army food, you tell them they're nuts. That's the best food in the world. If anybody has got a gripe against the Army food, they're fussy eaters. They would--they would knock any kind of--whatever they were eating, they would knock it. So--

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay. Is there anything else you'd like to add before we wrap it up?

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: No. I enjoyed my service. As a matter of fact, I'd like--I would have liked to stayed in 20 years active duty.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: But during the Korean War, I was married, and I was activated for three years, and there was no problems.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: Well, that's nice. Well, thank you very much.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Laughing} You're welcome.

sp.speaker: Christine Derby-Cuadrado
sp.p: And--thank you.

sp.speaker: Lawrence H. Vogel
sp.p: {Nods head}
